key_insight: A 2026 public charge rule could reduce immigrants’ use of primary care in NYC and increase premature mortality over both 5- and 20-year horizons.
clinical_relevance: Health systems and clinicians serving immigrant communities should anticipate coverage avoidance and possible downstream gaps in preventive and primary care access.
method: Deterministic compartmental simulation using ordinary differential equations.
Inputs from 2023 NYC vital statistics and American Community Survey data.
Modeled conservative, moderate, and aggressive chilling-effect scenarios using estimates from prior studies.
evidence_signal: Compared with a no-rule counterfactual, the model projected 4.1% to 9.9% lower primary care access and 4.4% to 17.4% higher premature mortality, depending on scenario and time horizon.
watch_item: Results are model-based and depend on prior-study effect estimates, so real-world impacts may differ if policy enforcement or avoidance behavior varies.
paper_title: The 2026 public charge rule and long-term health impacts among NYC immigrants: a simulation study
